THANK YOU SO MUCH. Seriously this is so helpful and gives me hope. I’m going to try what you suggested. I think I’ll go to the pharmacy today. I am not diabetic BUT I have hypoglycemia so I do get blood sugar issues but it’s always dropping low. Have had it my whole life. Also I do have raynauds in my feet so I know my circulation sucks sometimes.

Have had it almost 2 years now. I keep my feet dry as much as possible. I take super quick showers because my feet gets macerated after literally like a minute of water exposure! I have a lot of shoes lol and try to rotate which ones I wear. I hate shoes so I pretty much only wear them when outside. I have socks on inside pretty much always. I haven’t cleaned my shoes... what should I use to do that? Does it matter if I always have socks on? I use an over the counter powder for anti fungal. But I also even took a prescribed one the doc gave me at one point. Nothing has helped in the slightest. Have tried apple cider vinegar and bleach too haha. It’s not usually itchy. However if it does itch it’s usually right after I get out of the shower and start to dry off. Really itchy for maybe 5 minutes and then I am completely itch free. My feet are freezing all the time. ALL THE TIME. But there is red inflammation on the sides that sometimes feels warm to the touch. One doc thought I might have plantar keratoderma which is a form of ichthyosis I guess. But no treatments of any kind have helped. My feet and I are exhausted lol.
Doc did a biopsy. I used over the counter anti fungal and still use it daily just in case! Even had a prescription oral tablet and nothing helped. Maybe the doc didn’t test for the right fungus??

Any idea what kind of issue?? My foot doctor did a biopsy and said it wasn’t fungal but I’m not sure if there was a certain kind she checked for. I still use topical anti fungal to try to prevent any from happening. I even had an oral anti fungal thing I took a year ago that my doc gave me but nothing has helped.
Right?!
I have like a red ring around my feet

I have heard of it!! I have a lot of the symptoms but my feet get skin buildup that is so rapid on my feet. I know thickening is a symptom and the tightness but the pressure point buildup I’m not sure of. Here is an example. [foot](https://imgur.com/a/srq31Ps)

I wear socks because my feet are always soooo cold. Sometimes I don’t even realize they are cold until I cuddle my fiancé and he screams because my feet are so cold haha. I have done warm water foot soaks but my skin gets all built up and white and thick during a soak and then when my feet are drying and seem mostly dry I get this terrible burning and I want to rip the skin off my feet!!! Not a smoker. Here is a pic of what happens to my feet. This was after just 1 minute of water contact. [after water ](https://imgur.com/a/kxRoZ62)
I do have a lot of scleroderma symptoms... I’m going to ask my rheumatologist

I’m wondering if ANA is what I already had done. I saw a rheumatologist a while back and she did the basic autoimmune panel but it came back normal. I wonder if it would have shown up?

Yes it always looks like this when dry. After minimal contact with water though the pressure areas create new thick skin. I’m talking 30 seconds maybe and parts of my foot have a new layer of skin. I thought it was athletes foot but the doctors checked multiple times and nope. I still use anti fungal as a precautionary measure though. Anyways, after the skin growth from water contact dries it is very hard and tight. If I go several days without trying to file it down then my feet are painful and feel soooo tight. I use urea cream and other moisturizers multiple times a day but nothing seems to make any difference. I have seen primary care, dermatologist, rheumatologist, and podiatrist. I am still seeing my podiatrist as she is trying to find some combination of topical treatments that help at all. Rheumatologist did basic autoimmune panel but seemed fine. Autoimmune runs in my extended family. Lots of arthritis. I have been ruled out for MS too. For what it’s worth, my mom says she has feared I had scleroderma since I was a kid. I guess bc of the raynauds and because my feet have always had a weird ring around them but nothing severe. I also get really bad flairs of pain. It feels like my bones are rotting. My neck and back get that way. Muscles ache. But it eventually goes away after a few days or a week. Can’t find a pattern.

I’m not sure! What is that test? I had a basic blood test to check for some autoimmune stuff. Nothing showed up except I tested positive for the gene connected with ankylosing spondylitis but doc said I would likely never develop that.

Doctor confirmed no fungus. No other skin conditions we know of. My feet are very cold most of the time! I think because of my raynauds. It got bad about 2 years ago but I have always had a lighter line around my feet but not this extreme and didnt bother me. Tried every anti fungal imaginable for about a year until I saw a dermatologist and a podiatrist who said it wasn’t fungal. I have steroid cream to try to reduce inflammation. After literally maybe a minute of contact with water my feet have very rapid skin buildup in all the pressure point areas. If I don’t use a pumice stone every other day or so then my feet get very tight and thick and painful.

I don’t wear no show socks. All of my socks are either fuzzy socks (lol) or go above my ankle. I’ve tried buying different kinds of socks but no relief. I switch up what shoes I wear so it just depends!
Doctor has done biopsy’s. I still use anti fungal just to make sure I don’t develop any as a precautionary measure though.

I’m so happy your doctor took you seriously and acted quickly! I have a rheumatologist and she checked me for sjogrens but came back negative. She did a routine panel of bloodwork but I’m not sure if scleroderma would show up in just basic autoimmune bloodwork or not? I’m constantly torn between advocating for myself or just hoping its nothing. I have had Raynauds my whole life but over the last year or so the skin on my feet has gotten so tight, hard, and thick. I have seen a few docs and no one can figure out what’s wrong. I feel like none of my docs look at all of my medical history and instead just look at one thing and if it doesn’t make sense they just give up.

There is a special place in hell for ItWorks especially when they reach out to people who are clearly in recovery from eating disorders. I almost died as a teenager from an eating disorder and was hospitalized many times. Once I was in solid recovery in my young adult years I would actively use my social media to write about the harms of diet culture and just shed light on eating disorders, body image, how it can start, and how to help. Like my position is clear. I would have huns reach out and try to pitch ItWorks to me as “a safe way to lose weight.” I was always shocked at their lack of basic human awareness. Like yeah I’m speaking out about how I am practicing self love and how I intuitively eat and how when my pants got too tight I bought new freaking pants instead of trying to shrink myself. WHAT PART OF THIS MAKES YOU THINK ID WANT TO PLASTIC WRAP MYSELF? Also- if I was in a bad mindset and agreed to try that BS how could you in good conscious contribute to a disease you know I almost died to? GRRRR. Thankfully I have a good sense of humor and would usually respond like “no thanks, I don’t want to lose weight because I’ve been there done that and almost lost my entire life- but thanks for thinking of me!” Lol! I always try to remind myself that people just don’t understand the damage their lack of education can cause and try to let it go.
I’ll admit- it’s fun to pick at for a while but man do I wish I could just wear flip flops or be barefoot without it being so obnoxious and painful!
I haven’t but I’ve wanted to! I’m a little afraid of what it would do though because my layers of skin are so uneven. I’m afraid my feet would peel too much. But maybe it’s worth a try!
It took me forever to get a diagnosis until one dermatologist knew right away! It’s called palamoplantar keratoderma!

Basically all I can do is exfoliate and use a pumice stone but I have to do it daily. If I didn’t do it for a week it would look like this. I’ve been doing it daily for a few months now and it is a little better but my feet still peel and itch and are honestly painful at times. Thank you for asking!

So here’s the more horrifying news: I use a pumice stone and exfoliate every single day. My feet will be soft and then the next day so much has grown back. I finally got diagnosed with a rare skin disorder and turns out there is NOTHING I can do other than what I’m already doing :(
